items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I said that I didn't, because I knew right away what the deal was about.

ctx.x: We finished at the "Pump Room" the last of March and I came back to New York with Beezie who had come to Chicago to be with me the last two weeks. It was understood that we were to go back to the Cafe Society Uptown within six weeks time, so during the wait I did a few gigs.

One day I was standing on the steps of the house where I lived with my landlady and Beezie when a car drove up. Two fellows, one small and the other quite big got out of the car and asked if they could speak to me. We walked a couple of doors from my place and the little fellow asked me if I knew a woman named Sally. I said that I didn't, because I knew right away what the deal was about. Then they showed me a photo of Teddy's orchestra. The little guy told me that Sally was his wife and she had told him that she…

But I had a shoe to fit his foot because I pointed to Beezie and told him that she was my wife and that she had been with me in Chicago. That I could prove by her that the handwriting was not mine. If it had not been for that I suppose I would have gotten a good beating from the big fellow who must have been the small one's strong arm man.
